svg.title: OWASP Top 10 2025 mapped to LearnSphere ColdFusion
svg.desc: Ten cards list the OWASP Top 10 2025 categories with a short LearnSphere ColdFusion example for each risk.
svg.text: The Top 10 is an awareness baseline; use threat modeling and verification for complete coverage.

g.text: Broken Access Control
Learner changes a certificate ID; importer reaches an internal URL.
Deny by default; enforce ownership server-side; constrain outbound access.
Security Misconfiguration
Debug output, public CF Administrator, samples, or broad CORS.
Harden every layer and verify configuration continuously.
Software Supply Chain Failures
Unsupported CF/JDK, vulnerable JDBC driver, unverified build artifact.
Inventory, verify, scan, patch, and monitor vendor advisories.
Cryptographic Failures
Passwords use a fast hash; secrets are committed; TLS is optional.
Use approved primitives, managed keys, TLS, and data classification.
Injection
Course filters alter SQL, commands, LDAP, HTML, or expressions.
Parameterize data; allow-list identifiers; encode for output context.
Insecure Design
No abuse limits let bots mass-enroll or issue certificates.
Threat-model workflows; enforce invariants, quotas, and safe defaults.
Authentication Failures
Credential stuffing, weak recovery, session fixation, missing MFA.
Use vetted identity controls, throttling, MFA, and session rotation.
Software or Data Integrity Failures
Unsigned update, untrusted artifact, unsafe native deserialization.
Verify provenance and integrity; validate untrusted structured data.
Security Logging and Alerting Failures
Repeated access denials occur without useful logs or an alert.
Record safe events, protect logs, detect patterns, rehearse response.
Mishandling Exceptional Conditions
A timeout exposes a stack trace or accidentally allows enrollment.
Fail closed, centralize safe errors, bound resources, test failures.
